concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted earlier in this batch (manage-datasets.json). This page states the Workbench alone returns just the results array, stripped of the envelope every other surface returns.

concepts.label: Analytics Service API (query REST endpoint)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted earlier in this batch (query-params.json)

concepts.label: query response object
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already promoted. This page documents the Analytics-specific instance of the same envelope shape (requestID, clientContextID, signature, results, status, errors, warnings, metrics), plus two Analytics-only additions (plans, and a second, differently-scoped metrics object).

concepts.label: query error object
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already promoted. Analytics' version carries only code and msg, a narrower shape than n1ql's own (which also carries an optional reason detail, per the registry's own definition of this concept).

concepts.label: query request status (enumeration)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already promoted, but with a genuinely different member list on this page: 'success', 'running', 'failed', 'timeout', 'fatal' - Analytics has 'failed' where the registry's own definition of this enum lists 'errors' and 'stopped' instead, and Analytics has no 'stopped' value at all. Reused rather than forked because both are plainly the same kind of thing (a query's terminal/in-flight status) documented on sibling REST APIs, but the mismatch is real and recorded here rather than smoothed over - see cross_component_finding.

concepts.label: Analytics query plan object (Plans)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the Analytics-only response section (logicalPlan, optimizedLogicalPlan, rewrittenExpressionTree, expressionTree, job) with no Query-service equivalent on this page.

concepts.label: Analytics Metrics object (processedObjects)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a second, Analytics-only metrics object (currently just processedObjects) returned alongside the Common Metrics object this page also documents; see cross_component_finding for a documentation-quality note about the two metrics objects sharing identical prose.

relations.subject: n1ql:query-response-object
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (hasInternalComponent) - stretched from architectural part-whole to JSON-object field containment, same stretch as this batch's config.json/manage-datasets.json uses of similarly-shaped predicates.
relations.evidence: An array of error objects. Present only if 1 or more errors are returned during processing of the request.

relations.subject: n1ql:query-response-object
relations.evidence: An object containing the query plans, if requested.

relations.subject: analytics:workbench
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (doesNotSupport) - the Workbench deliberately withholds the envelope, returning bare results only.
relations.evidence: the Analytics Service returns a JSON array containing just the query results, separate from the query metrics or the query plan.

notable_absence.finding: The Common Metrics object and the Analytics-only Metrics object are given the exact same one-line description verbatim - 'An object containing metrics about the request.' - with nothing on the page distinguishing why a query response carries two separately-named metrics objects (one with six fields: elapsedTime/executionTime/resultCount/resultSize/errorCount/warningCount; one with a single field, processedObjects) rather than one merged object. A reader has to infer the split from the schema tables alone.

cross_component_finding: The promoted n1ql:query-request-status-enum is reused here for a genuinely different value set (Analytics: success/running/failed/timeout/fatal vs. the registry's own recorded success/running/errors/stopped/timeout/fatal), which is a third case this round of one nominally-shared REST concept fragmenting into incompatible concrete enums across API surfaces - alongside n1ql:scan-consistency's already-recorded Java-SDK subset and this round's own Analytics scan_consistency subset (query-params.json, this batch).
